questions.question_text: A 50-litre mixture contains acid and water in the ratio 4:1. After 3 litres of water are added, what is the new acid-to-water ratio?
questions.explanation: The original amounts are 40 L acid and 10 L water. After adding 3 L water, the ratio is 40:13, which is not among the listed ratios.
questions.source: Verified from supplied Mixture PDF, page 4; exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: A liquid has acid and water in the ratio 1:3. Adding 5 litres of acid changes the ratio to 1:2. What is the amount of the new mixture?
questions.explanation: If the original mixture is x litres, its acid and water amounts are x/4 and 3x/4. The equation (x/4+5):(3x/4)=1:2 gives x=40, so the new amount is 45 litres.
questions.source: Verified from supplied Mixture PDF, page 5; exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: Alcohol and water are mixed in the ratio 4:3. Adding 5 litres of water changes the ratio to 4:5. How much alcohol was in the original mixture?
questions.explanation: Let the original parts be 4k and 3k. Then 4k:(3k+5)=4:5, so k=2.5 and the alcohol amount is 4k=10 litres.
questions.source: Verified from supplied Mixture PDF, page 6; exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: A 9-kg dough has sugar and flour in the ratio 2:7. How much sugar must be added to make the sugar-to-flour ratio 2:5?
questions.explanation: The dough contains 2 kg sugar and 7 kg flour. For a 2:5 ratio, sugar must be 14/5=2.8 kg, so 0.8 kg or 800 g is added.
questions.source: Verified from supplied Mixture PDF, page 7; exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: A 100-g mixture contains 45% glycerine. If 35 g of water is added, what percentage of the new mixture is glycerine by weight?
questions.explanation: There are 45 g glycerine in 135 g of final mixture. The percentage is 45/135 x 100 = 33 1/3.
questions.source: Verified from supplied Mixture PDF, page 8; exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: An alloy contains 17.5 kg copper and zinc in the ratio 5:2. If 1.25 kg zinc is added, what is the new copper-to-zinc ratio?
questions.explanation: The original amounts are 12.5 kg copper and 5 kg zinc. After adding zinc, the ratio is 12.5:6.25=2:1.
questions.source: Verified from supplied Mixture PDF, page 9; exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: Two equal-capacity vessels contain water and milk in ratios 3:4 and 5:3. What is the water-to-milk ratio after combining their contents?
questions.explanation: Scale the first ratio to 24:32 and the second to 35:21. Adding components gives water:milk=59:53.
questions.source: Verified from supplied Mixture PDF, page 10; exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: Three equal-capacity bottles contain milk and water in ratios 5:7, 7:9 and 2:1. Their contents are poured together. Approximately what percentage of the final mixture is milk?
questions.explanation: Taking 48 units from each bottle gives milk amounts 20, 21 and 32, and water amounts 28, 27 and 16. Milk is 73/144 of the total, about 50.7%.
questions.source: Verified from supplied Mixture PDF, page 11; exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: Equal quantities are taken from four equal-capacity bottles whose milk-to-water ratios are 1:2, 2:3, 3:2 and 7:8. What is the final milk-to-water ratio?
questions.explanation: For equal quantities, the milk fractions sum to 1/3+2/5+3/5+7/15=27/15 and the water fractions to 33/15. The ratio is 9:11.
questions.source: Verified from supplied Mixture PDF, page 12; exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: Two rum-and-soda solutions have ratios 2:3 and 3:2. They are mixed in the quantity ratio 4:1. What is the resulting rum-to-soda ratio?
questions.explanation: Five equal parts of the first and one part of the second give rum:soda=(2x4+3):(3x4+2)=11:14.
questions.source: Verified from supplied Mixture PDF, page 13; exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: Three glasses hold 3 L, 4 L and 5 L. Their milk-to-water ratios are 2:3, 3:7 and 4:11. What is the milk-to-water ratio after combining them?
questions.explanation: The milk amounts are 6/5, 6/5 and 4/3 L; water amounts are 9/5, 14/5 and 11/3 L. Their ratio reduces from 56:124 to 14:31.
questions.source: Verified from supplied Mixture PDF, page 14; exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: One liquid contains 20% water and another contains 35% water. Ten parts of the first and four parts of the second are mixed. What percentage of the blend is water?
questions.explanation: The water amount is 10(0.20)+4(0.35)=3.4 parts in 14 parts total. Thus water is 3.4/14 x 100=24 2/7%.
questions.source: Verified from supplied Mixture PDF, page 15; exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: Two alloys contain copper and tin in ratios 1:3 and 2:5. In what quantity ratio should the first and second alloys be mixed to obtain tin:copper = 8:3?
questions.explanation: Copper fractions are 1/4 and 2/7; the target copper fraction is 3/11. Alligation gives first:second=(3/11-2/7):(1/4-3/11)=4:7.
questions.source: Verified from supplied Mixture PDF, page 16; exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: A laboratory has acid-water solutions in ratios 2:5 and 7:3. In what quantity ratio should the first and second solutions be mixed to obtain acid:water = 2:3?
questions.explanation: The acid fractions are 2/7 and 7/10; the target is 2/5. Alligation gives first:second=(7/10-2/5):(2/5-2/7)=21:8.
questions.source: Verified from supplied Mixture PDF, page 17; exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: Two vessels contain petrol and kerosene in ratios 4:3 and 3:5. In what quantity ratio should portions from the first and second vessels be mixed so the resulting amounts of petrol and kerosene are equal?
questions.explanation: The petrol fractions differ from one-half by 1/14 above and 1/8 below. The required first:second quantity ratio is 1/8:1/14=7:4.
questions.source: Verified from supplied Mixture PDF, page 18; exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: Vessel A contains milk and water in ratio 4:3; vessel B has them in ratio 2:3. What quantity ratio A:B gives a blend that is half milk and half water?
questions.explanation: Milk fractions are 4/7 and 2/5, and the target is 1/2. Alligation gives A:B=(1/2-2/5):(4/7-1/2)=7:5.
questions.source: Verified from supplied Mixture PDF, page 19; exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: Twelve litres of a milk-water mixture have ratio 3:1. Eight litres of another have ratio 1:3. What is the final milk-to-water ratio?
questions.explanation: The milk amounts are 9 and 2 L, and the water amounts are 3 and 6 L. Thus the ratio is 11:9.

questions.question_text: A 20-L acid-water mixture is 2:3. How many litres of water should be added to make the ratio 8:17?
questions.explanation: There are 8 L acid and 12 L water. For acid:water=8:17, water must be 17 L, so add 5 L.

questions.question_text: A 30-kg sugar-flour dough has sugar:flour=1:4. How much sugar must be added so the final ratio is 2:5?
questions.explanation: There are 6 kg sugar and 24 kg flour. The target sugar amount is 2/5 x 24=9.6 kg, requiring 3.6 kg more.

questions.question_text: A 40-L drink contains juice and water in ratio 3:5. How much pure juice must be added to make equal amounts of juice and water?
questions.explanation: The drink has 15 L juice and 25 L water. Adding 10 L juice makes both amounts 25 L.

questions.question_text: A grocer blends 20 kg of rice costing Rs 20/kg with 30 kg costing Rs 30/kg. What is the average cost per kilogram?
questions.explanation: The total cost is 20x20+30x30=Rs 1,300 for 50 kg, or Rs 26/kg.

questions.question_text: A 12-L solution is 25% syrup and an 8-L solution is 50% syrup. What is the syrup percentage after mixing?
questions.explanation: The syrup amounts are 3 L and 4 L. Seven litres in 20 L is 35%.

questions.question_text: A 32-kg brass ingot has copper:zinc=5:3. How many kilograms of zinc does it contain?
questions.explanation: There are 8 ratio parts, so each part is 4 kg. Zinc is 3 parts, or 12 kg.

questions.question_text: Five kilograms of a solution is 40% salt; another 15 kg solution is 20% salt. Find the salt percentage of the blend.
questions.explanation: Salt totals 2+3=5 kg in 20 kg mixture, which is 25%.

questions.question_text: A 20-L milk-water mixture is 7:3. How much water must be added to make the ratio 7:5?
questions.explanation: Milk is 14 L and water 6 L. The target water amount is 10 L, so add 4 L.

questions.question_text: A 16-L milk-water mixture has ratio 3:5. How much milk must be added to make milk and water equal?
questions.explanation: It contains 6 L milk and 10 L water. Add 4 L milk to equalize them.

questions.question_text: Four kilograms of tea costing Rs 300/kg are blended with 6 kg costing Rs 450/kg. Find the blend cost per kilogram.
questions.explanation: Total cost is Rs 1,200+2,700=3,900 for 10 kg, giving Rs 390/kg.

questions.question_text: Eight litres of alcohol solution is 30% alcohol. How much water should be added to reduce it to 20%?
questions.explanation: Alcohol remains 2.4 L. At 20%, the total volume must be 12 L, so add 4 L water.

questions.question_text: How many kilograms of a 35% concentrate must be mixed with 10 kg of a 15% concentrate to obtain a 25% blend?
questions.explanation: The target lies midway between 15% and 35%, so equal quantities are required: 10 kg.

questions.question_text: A 35-kg alloy has copper:tin=3:4. After adding 5 kg tin, what is the new copper-to-tin ratio?
questions.explanation: Copper is 15 kg and tin 20 kg; after addition tin is 25 kg, giving 3:5.

questions.question_text: A 24-kg milk-water mixture has milk:water=5:3. How many kilograms of milk does it contain?
questions.explanation: Eight ratio parts equal 24 kg, so one part is 3 kg and milk is 5x3=15 kg.

questions.question_text: Equal volumes of two drinks with water:milk ratios 2:3 and 3:2 are combined. What is the final water-to-milk ratio?
questions.explanation: The water fractions are 2/5 and 3/5, whose equal-weight average is 1/2; milk is also 1/2.

questions.question_text: How much sugar is present in 25 L of a 12% sugar solution?
questions.explanation: Twelve percent of 25 L is 3 L of sugar.

questions.question_text: Five litres of 60% acid solution are mixed with 15 litres of 20% acid solution. What is the final acid percentage?
questions.explanation: The acid totals 3+3=6 L in 20 L, so the concentration is 30%.

questions.question_text: Thirty kilograms of grain costing Rs 80/kg are mixed with 20 kg costing Rs 110/kg. Find the mean cost per kilogram.
questions.explanation: The total cost is Rs 2,400+2,200=4,600 for 50 kg, or Rs 92/kg.

questions.question_text: A 40-L milk-water mixture is 3:5. If 8 litres are poured out, how many litres of milk remain?
questions.explanation: The mixture contains 15 L milk. The 8-L portion contains 3 L milk, leaving 12 L milk.

questions.question_text: Six kilograms of nuts at Rs 120/kg are mixed with 4 kg at Rs 180/kg. What is the average price per kilogram?
questions.explanation: The total cost is Rs 720+720=1,440 for 10 kg, or Rs 144/kg.

questions.question_text: Twenty litres of a 30% concentrate are diluted by removing 5 litres of the mixture and replacing it with water. What is the new concentration?
questions.explanation: The initial concentrate is 6 L. Removing 5 L removes 1.5 L concentrate, leaving 4.5 L in 20 L, or 22.5%.

questions.question_text: A vessel holds 12 L of pure milk. How much water must be added for milk:water to become 3:1?
questions.explanation: One quarter of the final 16 L is water, so add 4 L.

questions.question_text: Fifteen litres of 40% salt solution are combined with 5 litres of 10% salt solution. What is the final salt percentage?
questions.explanation: Salt totals 6+0.5=6.5 L-equivalent in 20 L, which is 32.5%.

questions.question_text: Six litres of acid-water solution have ratio 2:1; nine litres of another solution have ratio 1:2. What is the combined acid-to-water ratio?
questions.explanation: Acid totals 4+3=7 L and water totals 2+6=8 L.

questions.question_text: A trader blends 20% and 50% acid solutions to obtain a 32% solution. What is the required quantity ratio, weaker solution:stronger solution?
questions.explanation: By alligation, weaker:stronger=(50-32):(32-20)=18:12=3:2.

questions.question_text: Coffee at Rs 240/kg is mixed with coffee at Rs 360/kg to obtain a blend worth Rs 300/kg. What quantity ratio gives this price?
questions.explanation: The target price is halfway between Rs 240 and Rs 360, so equal quantities are needed.

questions.question_text: A 60-L vessel is full of milk. Twelve litres are removed and replaced with water. What is the final milk-to-water ratio?
questions.explanation: After removal, 48 L milk remains and 12 L water is added, giving 4:1.

questions.question_text: An 80-L mixture has milk:water=7:3. Twenty litres are withdrawn and replaced with water. What is the new milk-to-water ratio?
questions.explanation: The withdrawn amount contains 14 L milk and 6 L water. Remaining amounts are 42 L milk and 18 L water; add 20 L water to get 42:38=21:19.

questions.question_text: Twenty-five kilograms of 12% solution are blended with 35 kg of 32% solution. What is the final concentration?
questions.explanation: Solute totals 3+11.2=14.2 kg in 60 kg, so concentration is 23 2/3%.

questions.question_text: How many kilograms each of 30% and 50% acid solutions make 40 kg of a 42% blend? Give the amount of the 50% solution.
questions.explanation: Alligation gives weaker:stronger=(50-42):(42-30)=2:3. Three fifths of 40 kg is 24 kg.

questions.question_text: Fifteen litres of 40% acid solution are mixed with a 10% solution to make a 25% solution. How many litres of the weaker solution are needed?
questions.explanation: Solve (6+0.1x)/(15+x)=0.25; this gives 0.15x=2.25 and x=15 L.

questions.question_text: A 35-kg alloy contains copper and zinc in ratio 3:4. How much zinc must be added to make copper:zinc=3:5?
questions.explanation: The alloy has 15 kg copper and 20 kg zinc. The target requires 25 kg zinc, so add 5 kg.

questions.question_text: A 50-L alcohol solution is 30% alcohol. Ten litres are removed and replaced with pure alcohol. What is the new alcohol percentage?
questions.explanation: The initial 15 L alcohol loses 3 L when 10 L mixture is removed, then gains 10 L. Thus 22/50=44%.

questions.question_text: A 100-kg blend is made from 20 kg of 10% solution, 30 kg of 40% solution and 50 kg of 60% solution. Find its concentration.
questions.explanation: Solute totals 2+12+30=44 kg in 100 kg, giving 44%.

questions.question_text: Thirty litres of milk-water mixture are 2:1, and 15 litres of another are 1:2. What is the final milk-to-water ratio?
questions.explanation: The first contributes 20 L milk and 10 L water; the second contributes 5 L each. The total ratio is 25:20=5:4.

questions.question_text: Coffee at Rs 350/kg is mixed with coffee at Rs 500/kg to average Rs 410/kg. If 15 kg of the cheaper coffee is used, how much of the dearer coffee is needed?
questions.explanation: Alligation gives cheaper:dearer=(500-410):(410-350)=3:2. Thus 15 kg corresponds to 10 kg dearer coffee.

questions.question_text: How much water must be added to 40 L of a 45% solution to reduce its concentration to 30%?
questions.explanation: There are 18 L solute. At 30%, the final volume must be 60 L, requiring 20 L water.

questions.question_text: A 25-kg mixture is 12% salt. How much pure salt must be added to make it 20% salt?
questions.explanation: Solve (3+x)/(25+x)=0.20, giving 0.8x=2 and x=2.5 kg.

questions.question_text: Eight litres of a 75% solution are combined with 12 litres of a 25% solution. What is the final concentration?
questions.explanation: The solute amounts are 6 and 3 L. Nine litres in 20 L is 45%.

questions.question_text: A 48-kg blend uses two rice varieties costing Rs 120/kg and Rs 180/kg. The mean price is Rs 150/kg. How much of the dearer variety is used?
questions.explanation: The target is midway between the prices, so half of 48 kg, or 24 kg, is the dearer variety.

questions.question_text: One hundred litres of 40% solution have 25 L removed and replaced with 20% solution. What is the new concentration?
questions.explanation: Solute falls from 40 L to 30 L after removal, then rises by 5 L to 35 L in 100 L.

questions.question_text: A 36-L vessel contains pure milk. Nine litres are removed and replaced with water; the same operation is repeated once. What is the final milk:water ratio?
questions.explanation: After two rounds milk is 36(27/36)^2=20.25 L; water is 15.75 L. The ratio is 9:7.

questions.question_text: Equal amounts of three solutions containing 20%, 40% and 70% solute are combined. What is the final concentration?
questions.explanation: For equal amounts, concentration is the mean: (20+40+70)/3=43 1/3%.

questions.question_text: A 60-kg salt-sand mixture has salt:sand=5:7. How much salt must be added to make the ratio 3:4?
questions.explanation: There are 25 kg salt and 35 kg sand. At 3:4, salt must be 26.25 kg, so add 1.25 kg.

questions.question_text: A 40-L milk-water mixture is 3:5. How much pure milk must be added to make the ratio 3:4?
questions.explanation: There are 15 L milk and 25 L water. Solve (15+x):25=3:4 to get x=3.75 L.

questions.question_text: Solutions of 24% and 44% concentration are blended in volume ratio 5:3. What is the resulting concentration?
questions.explanation: The weighted concentration is (24x5+44x3)/8=31.5%.

questions.question_text: A 25-L mixture is 32% concentrate. Some is removed and replaced with a 12% solution. If the final concentration is 28%, how many litres were replaced?
questions.explanation: Solute after replacement is 0.32(25-x)+0.12x. Setting this to 0.28x25 gives x=5 L.

questions.question_text: An 80-L mixture is 60% concentrate. Ten litres are replaced with water, and this operation is repeated. What is the final concentration?
questions.explanation: Each operation leaves 7/8 of the concentrate. Final concentrate is 48(7/8)^2=36.75 L in 80 L, or 45.9375%.

questions.question_text: A 100-L solution is 50% acid. First 20 L are replaced with water; then 10 L of the new mixture are also replaced with water. Find the final acid percentage.
questions.explanation: After the first exchange acid is 40 L. The second removes 4 L acid, leaving 36 L in 100 L.

questions.question_text: A 100-L solution contains 48% acid. Replace 25 L with a 20% acid solution, then replace 20 L of the new mixture with water. What is the final concentration?
questions.explanation: After the first exchange acid is 36+5=41 L. The next removal leaves 41x80/100=32.8 L acid in 100 L.

questions.question_text: A blend contains 20 kg of 70% copper alloy, 30 kg of 40% copper alloy, and some pure copper. How much pure copper is needed for a 60% copper blend?
questions.explanation: Copper is initially 14+12=26 kg. Solve (26+x)/(50+x)=0.60 to get x=10 kg.

questions.question_text: Two coffees cost Rs 220/kg and Rs 340/kg. Their blend averages Rs 300/kg, and the dearer coffee exceeds the cheaper by 20 kg. Find the total blend weight.
questions.explanation: Alligation gives cheaper:dearer=(340-300):(300-220)=1:2. Their difference is one part, or 20 kg; total is three parts=60 kg.

questions.question_text: Three solutions are mixed in quantity ratio 3:2:1. The first is 40% solute and the second is 70%. What concentration must the third solution have for the blend to be 50%?
questions.explanation: The first two contribute 3(40)+2(70)=260 concentration-parts. For six total parts at 50%, the third must contribute 300-260=40, so it is 40%.

questions.question_text: A 60-L milk-water mixture has ratio 5:3. Twelve litres are removed and replaced with pure milk. What is the final milk-to-water ratio?
questions.explanation: Initially milk=37.5 L and water=22.5 L. Removing 12 L removes 7.5 and 4.5 L; after adding milk, amounts are 42 and 18 L, or 7:3.

questions.question_text: A 40-L liquid is 40% solute. It is mixed with a 70% solution. How many litres of the stronger solution are needed for a 52% blend?
A 60-L solution is 50% concentrate. Replace 15 L with a 20% solution, then repeat the same exchange. What is the final concentration?
questions.explanation: After one exchange concentrate is 30-7.5+3=25.5 L. After the second it is 25.5-6.375+3=22.125 L, which is 36.875% of 60 L.

questions.question_text: A mixture has 30 L of 20% solution, 45 L of 50% solution and 15 L of 80% solution. What is its overall concentration?
questions.explanation: Solute totals 6+22.5+12=40.5 L in 90 L, giving 45%.

questions.question_text: A 75-L solution is 24% solute. Replace 15 L with a 60% solution. What is the new concentration?
questions.explanation: Initially solute is 18 L. The exchange removes 3.6 L and adds 9 L, leaving 23.4 L in 75 L, or 31.2%.

questions.question_text: An 80-L milk-water mixture has ratio 3:5. Remove 16 L of the mixture, then add pure milk until the ratio becomes 2:3. How much milk is added?
questions.explanation: After removal, milk=24 L and water=40 L. Solve (24+x):40=2:3, giving x=8/3, about 2.6667 L.

questions.question_text: Twenty-four litres of 25% solution are mixed with a 55% solution to obtain 40%. If 12 L of the blend are then removed, how much solute remains?
questions.explanation: The alligation equation gives 24 L of the stronger solution. The blend has 19.2 L solute in 48 L; after removing one-quarter, 14.4 L remains.

questions.question_text: Solutions are mixed in quantity ratio 1:2:2. Their concentrations are 20%, 50% and x%. If the blend is 42%, find x.
Two alloys contain tin:copper in ratios 2:3 and 1:4. In what ratio should the first and second alloys be combined to obtain tin:copper=1:2?
questions.explanation: Tin fractions are 2/5 and 1/5; the target is 1/3. Alligation yields first:second=(1/3-1/5):(2/5-1/3)=2:1.

questions.question_text: A 120-L mixture is 35% alcohol. Replace 30 L with an x% alcohol solution, then replace 20 L of the new mixture with water. If the final concentration is 30%, find x.
questions.explanation: After the first exchange alcohol is 31.5+0.3x L. The second leaves 5/6 of it; setting that to 36 L gives x=39%.

questions.question_text: A tank has 25 L of 60% concentrate and 15 L of 20% concentrate. How much water must be added to reduce the final concentration to 35%?
questions.explanation: The solute is 15+3=18 L in 40 L. Solve 18/(40+x)=0.35, giving x=80/7, about 11.4286 L.

questions.question_text: Twenty litres of a 25% solution and 30 litres of a 40% solution are mixed with x litres of a 70% solution. If the final concentration is 50%, find x.
questions.explanation: Solute equation: 5+12+0.7x=0.5(50+x). Thus 0.2x=8 and x=40 L.

questions.question_text: A 60-kg alloy has copper:zinc=7:5. How much zinc must be added to make copper:zinc=7:8?
questions.explanation: Copper is 35 kg and zinc 25 kg. The target requires 40 kg zinc, so add 15 kg.

questions.question_text: A 50-L solution is 40% acid. Ten litres are removed and replaced with water. How much pure acid must then be added to restore a 40% concentration?
questions.explanation: After replacement, 16 L acid remains. Solve (16+x)/(50+x)=0.40, yielding x=20/3, about 6.6667 L.

questions.question_text: A 60-L blend contains 25% solute. How much 50% solution must be added to make the blend 45%?
A mixture contains 20 kg of 30% solution and 30 kg of 50% solution. How many kilograms of water must evaporate for the concentration to become 50%?
questions.explanation: Solute remains 6+15=21 kg. At 50%, the total mass must be 42 kg; evaporate 50-42=8 kg water.

questions.question_text: A 100-L solution is 80% milk. Replace 20 L with water, then remove 10 L of the new mixture and replace it with pure milk. What is the final milk percentage?
questions.explanation: After the first exchange milk is 64 L. The next removal leaves 57.6 L milk; adding 10 L gives 67.6 L in 100 L.

questions.question_text: One hundred litres of 50% solution are repeatedly replaced with a 20% solution: first 20 L, then 10 L. What is the final solute percentage?
questions.explanation: First solute amount becomes 50-10+4=44 L. Next it becomes 44-4.4+2=41.6 L in 100 L, hence 41.6%.

questions.question_text: An alloy blend contains 40 kg of 25% copper alloy and 60 kg of 55% copper alloy. How much pure tin must be added to reduce copper to 40%?
questions.explanation: Copper is 10+33=43 kg. At 40%, total mass must be 43/0.4=107.5 kg, so add 7.5 kg tin.

questions.question_text: A 40-L solution is 25% acid. It is mixed with some 55% acid solution, then 10 L of water is added. If the final concentration is 35%, how much 55% solution was used?
questions.explanation: If x litres of the stronger solution are used, (10+0.55x)/(50+x)=0.35. Solving 0.2x=7.5 gives x=37.5 L.
